description: Wait until a release is 3 days old before raising its update, for every datasource that reports release timestamps. Malware scanners and registries get time to find and pull a bad release, and Renovate creates no branch and runs no package manager on it before then (internalChecksFilter defaults to strict). Security updates skip the wait: vulnerabilityAlerts sets minimumReleaseAge to null.

packageRules.description: Datasources with release timestamps (releaseTimestampSupport in Renovate 44). docker is left out: it has timestamps only on Docker Hub, and the default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour (timestamp-required) would hold images from mcr.microsoft.com, ghcr.io or ACR forever. Datasources without timestamps (git-tags, git-refs, azure-pipelines-tasks, azure-bicep-resource, ...) are left out for the same reason.
Lock file maintenance has no release timestamp: the package manager picks the versions
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ Lock file maintenance does not check the 3-day minimum release age: the package manager picks the versions. Check that no version in this PR is younger than 3 days.

packageRules.description: Replacements and pinning do not carry the release age (renovatebot/renovate#39400, #40288)
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ Renovate does not check the 3-day minimum release age for replacements and pinning. Check that no version in this PR is younger than 3 days.

packageRules.description: bump, lockfileUpdate and rollback updates have no release timestamp
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ Renovate does not check the 3-day minimum release age for `bump`, `lockfileUpdate` and `rollback` updates. Check that no version in this PR is younger than 3 days.
